info.album: I Can See Clearly Now (Expanded Edition)

podcast.body: This song was included by critic Greal Marcus in his list of strong and clear records from the early 1970s that constituted a significant and unified musical answer from black artists. "Johnny Nash I can see clearly now."

srcs.episode: Ep. 22 - Power to the People - The Music of the Black Power Movement
Ep. 22 - Power to the People - The Music of the Black Power Movement

podcast.body: Written and performed by Johnny Nash, this song is widely recognized as the first "reggae-ish" number one hit in the United States, topping the charts on November 4, 1972, and maintaining its position for an entire month before being unseated by The Temptations' "Papa Was a Rolling Stone." "However, the song that many considered the first reggae-ish number one in the United States is a song that Nash wrote himself. I Can See Clearly Now."
